Thanks again for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have clear owners.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: document understanding + reranking pipeline (embeddings -> candidate gen -> reranker -> structured output).
- Peak: ~900 QPS sustained during business hours, bursts up to ~2.5k QPS for 20-30 min windows.
- Latency SLO: 200-400ms 95th p50 depends on model/route; reranker path can tolerate up to 800ms in some flows.
- Auth: SSO for human users; server-to-server traffic will use API keys / mTLS for ingestion.
- SDK: Plan to use Redwood SDK for streaming + function/tool calling for structured output.

Open items / next steps
1) Acme to share QPS profile and sample payloads (Bethany) - helps size batching + KV cache behavior. (action: Bethany, due: 2/23)
2) Redwood to propose initial dedicated-capacity sizing and autoscale policy (action: Aditya + Marissa, due: 2/24)

4) Security/procurement checklist (Acme to share any compliance docs) - we can loop SRE/security as needed. (action: Bethany)

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing - post-call next steps

Thanks for the profile, Bethany - looks helpful. A few initial recommendations from an infra perspective (high level) so the deep-dive is more productive:

Sizing / autoscale
- Baseline: to cover steady 900 QPS with headroom for model warmup/batching, recommend an initial pool of 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent vCPU-backed pods if using CPU models).
- Autoscale policy: scale in increments of 2 GPUs, cooldown 5m, max pool to handle 2.5k QPS bursts to 24 GPUs (depends on model/quantization).
- Warm standby: maintain a small warm buffer (1-2 instances) to reduce cold-start tail latency for burst windows.

Throughput / concurrency / queues
- Concurrency per worker: limit to ~8-12 concurrent sessions depending on model context window to avoid memory thrashing.
- Request queue: introduce a short in-cluster FIFO queue with a configurable max wait (eg 500ms) before we trigger a degraded path / fallback to a cheaper model. This keeps latency SLOs stable under burst.
- Batching: enable dynamic batching with a max batch size tuned from the QPS profile - aim for batch sizes that keep GPU utilization >70% while keeping P95 latency within SLO.

Caching & embeddings/rerankers
- Prefix/KV cache: aggressively cache common prefixes for user prompts and include a small per-shard KV cache to reduce repeated compute on candidate generation.
- Embeddings: do embeddings offline for historical dataset and store vectors in your vector DB; use real-time embedding for user-provided text only.
- Reranker: run reranker on a smaller candidate set (n=20-50) and measure tradeoff between recall and latency - can shard reranker across a separate pool to isolate CPU/GPU contention.

Integration notes (SDK & auth)
- SDK: use Redwood SDK streaming for the generator stage, and function/tool calling for structured outputs. Sample snippet:
  // pseudo
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  const stream = client.responses.stream({ model: 'redwood-gen-v1', max_tokens: 256 });

- Auth: we support API keys with optional mutual TLS for server-to-server; tie API keys to project IDs so we can route requests to the correct dedicated pool.

References & links
- Draft architecture diagram: https://drive.google.com/acme/redwood-dedicated-arch-diagram
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1347

I will put together a short sizing doc and an initial autoscale policy proposal by 2/24. Happy to go deeper in the scheduled deep-dive.
